policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'kept back by fraud' renders either compound equally; ἀφυστερέω and ἀποστερέω are both 'withhold/defraud' here and the English shows no orthographic or semantic trace of which stem stood. No note is mapped to this unit.
The variants differ only in the perfect active ending (-ασιν vs -αν) of the same verb; 'have entered' renders both identically. Nothing in the ASV or its notes distinguishes them.

ASV reads 'ye have nourished your hearts in a day of slaughter' with no comparative particle. The RP addition of ὡς would require 'as in a day of slaughter'; the absence of 'as' in the ASV, unitalicized and unnoted, distinguishes the shorter reading.

ἐπ᾽ αὐτῷ and ἐπ᾽ αὐτόν are both rendered 'over it'; the case of the object of ἐπί leaves no mark in English. The 'Or, he' note is classed alternative_rendering and concerns the English pronoun's referent, not the reading.

ASV 'until it receive the early and latter rain' supplies the head noun 'rain' that both readings require in English: the shorter text has the adjectives alone, the RP reading spells out ὑετόν. The verse shows no italic supply or mapped textual note to separate them.

ASV 'Murmur not, brethren, one against another' places the vocative before the prepositional phrase, which excludes the RP order κατ᾽ ἀλλήλων ἀδελφοί (r02). The remaining two readings differ only in the comma after ἀδελφοί, a punctuation matter the English cannot decide.
ASV reads 'Take, brethren, for an example' without a possessive, where the same translators render μου as 'My brethren' at 5:19. The bare vocative distinguishes the reading lacking μου.
With or without ἐν, the dative τῷ ὀνόματι is rendered 'in the name' in English; the preposition's presence leaves no trace. No note is mapped here.

ASV 'them that endured' is past, rendering the aorist participle ὑπομείναντας; the RP present ὑπομένοντας would give 'them that endure'. The 'Or, endurance' note is alternative_rendering and belongs to ὑπομονήν, not this unit.
ASV 'and have seen the end of the Lord' is a second-person indicative parallel to 'ye have heard', which renders εἴδετε; the RP ἴδετε is an imperative that would require 'and see'.
ASV supplies an express subject, 'how that the Lord is full of pity, and merciful', which renders ὁ κύριος; the RP omission leaves only an unexpressed 'he is'.
ASV 'that ye fall not under judgment' renders ὑπὸ κρίσιν; the RP εἰς ὑπόκρισιν would give 'into hypocrisy'. The alternative_rendering note concerns the yea/nay clause and does not bear on this unit.

ASV 'anointing him with oil' has an express object, unitalicized, which renders αὐτόν; the WH omission leaves the participle without one. The 'Or, having anointed' note concerns the participle's tense, not the object.
ASV 'Confess therefore your sins' carries an inferential connective rendering οὖν, which the RP reading omits.
ASV reads 'your sins', the ASV's standing rendering of ἁμαρτίαι; παράπτωμα is rendered 'trespass' by these translators, so the noun chosen distinguishes the base reading.
εὔχεσθε and προσεύχεσθε are both rendered 'pray'; the simplex and compound are not distinguished in the ASV's English, and no note is mapped here.
The readings differ only in the order of verb and object; English requires 'the heaven gave rain' either way, so the ASV cannot distinguish them.
ASV opens 'My brethren', an unitalicized possessive rendering μου, which the RP reading omits.

ASV text reads 'let him know', the third-person imperative γινωσκέτω, and the mapped textual_variant note 'Some ancient authorities read know ye' places the RP γινώσκετε in the margin rather than the text.
ASV 'from the error of his way' has an unitalicized possessive rendering αὐτοῦ; the omitting reading would give 'the error of the way'. The verse's textual note concerns γινωσκέτω, not this unit.
